title: Florida condo market in October 2026: sales fell 5%, the median slipped to $290,000, and buyers gained ground
seoTitle: Florida Condo Market, October 2026: Sales and Prices
description: Florida condo-townhouse sales fell 5% in October 2026, the median dropped 3.3% to $290,000 and supply hit 8 months. What it means for owners and boards.
dek: The new statewide numbers from Florida Realtors show condo sales cooling as mortgage rates rose, prices easing, and buyers holding more of the cards than they did a month ago.
facebook: Wondering what your Florida condo would sell for today? October's statewide numbers are out: sales down 5%, the median down 3.3% to $290,000, and eight months of supply. Here's what that means in plain words, and what buyers will ask about your building.
keywords: is it a buyers market for Florida condos

body.text: Every month, Florida Realtors adds up condo and townhouse sales from the state's multiple listing services, the shared databases real estate agents use to list homes. The October 2026 numbers came out on Monday, November 16. They give owners and boards a quick statewide picture: how many units sold, what they sold for, and how many are still waiting for a buyer.

These are statewide totals for condos and townhouses together. Your building and your town can look very different. But the big picture shapes what buyers expect when they walk into your lobby, so it is worth a few minutes at the kitchen table.
All of these compare October 2026 with October 2025.

items: Closed sales: 6,862 condos and townhouses sold, down 5%. A closed sale is one where the deal is finished and the keys have changed hands.
Median sale price: $290,000, down 3.3%. The median is the middle price: half of the units sold for more, half for less.
New pending sales: 6,730 units went under contract, down 11.9%. A pending sale is a signed contract that has not closed yet.
Active listings: 61,983 condos and townhouses were for sale, down 8.8%.

body.title: What “months of supply” means
body.text: Months of supply estimates how long it would take to sell every unit now on the market at the recent pace of sales, if no new listings came in. The higher the number, the more choices buyers have and the more room they have to bargain. The lower it is, the more the market leans toward sellers.

A month earlier, Florida Realtors reported a September median of $293,500 and 7.7 months of supply. So in one month the statewide median slipped by $3,500 and supply rose from 7.7 to 8 months. Listings also ticked up, from 60,367 at the end of September to 61,983 at the end of October.

There are still fewer condos for sale than a year ago. But sales and new contracts are slowing faster than listings are falling. That is why buyers have a little more breathing room than they did in September.

Florida Realtors says higher mortgage rates slowed sales across the state in October. Its chief economist, Dr. Brad O'Connor, put it this way: “The condo and townhouse market is facing somewhat greater pricing pressure.” He also said condo-townhouse prices “reflected the greater supply available to buyers in that segment of the market.”

Single-family homes told a different story. Their sales fell 10.1%, but their median price rose 2.2% to $420,000, and they had 4.6 months of supply. In plain words: houses are selling more slowly but holding their price, while condos are giving a little on price.

Looking ahead, Florida Realtors says O'Connor expects closed sales to keep running below last year for another month or two, as the slower pace of new contracts works its way through. He said that if mortgage rates stay above 7%, sales should stay subdued and inventory should slowly build. If rates move lower, he said, there is still plenty of pent-up demand on the sidelines.
What to do with these numbers

items: If you plan to sell, look at your own area and your own building, not just the state. A local agent can pull recent sales near you, and Florida Realtors also publishes numbers by metro area.
Price for a market where buyers can shop. With eight months of supply statewide, many buyers can compare several units before they make an offer.

Get your building's paperwork ready before you list. Buyers and their lenders often ask about the budget, the reserves, recent inspections and any special assessments. Ask your manager now where those documents are and how to get copies.
If you are not selling, don't panic over one month. A statewide median moves for many reasons, including which units happened to sell that month.

body.text: If you are on the board:

items: Remember that your building's records are part of every owner's sale. Clear, current information on the budget, reserves and repairs helps owners answer buyers quickly.
Share plain facts with owners. A short note about what the building has done and what is planned can save owners, buyers and agents a lot of guessing.

Send questions about what a sale disclosure must include to the association attorney, and questions about the building's condition to the engineer. The board's job is to keep the records accurate and available.

body.text: Florida Realtors' schedule lists Wednesday, December 16, 2026, as the release date for the November numbers.

faq.q: Are Florida condo prices going down?
faq.a: In October 2026 the statewide median condo-townhouse price was $290,000, down 3.3% from October 2025, according to Florida Realtors. The September 2026 median was $293,500.

faq.q: Is it a buyers market for Florida condos right now?
faq.a: Buyers have more room to bargain. Condos and townhouses had 8 months of supply in October 2026, up from 7.7 in September. Florida Realtors' chief economist said that supply gives buyers more negotiating room.

faq.q: How many condos are for sale in Florida?
faq.a: Florida Realtors counted 61,983 active condo and townhouse listings statewide in October 2026, down 8.8% from a year earlier.

faq.q: Why are Florida condo sales slowing?
faq.a: Florida Realtors says higher mortgage rates slowed sales in October 2026. Condo-townhouse closed sales fell 5% and new contracts fell 11.9% compared with October 2025.

faq.q: When do the next Florida condo market numbers come out?
faq.a: Florida Realtors' research schedule lists Wednesday, December 16, 2026, for the November 2026 numbers.
